svg.title: PostgreSQL and Redis differ most on durability model and primary operational constraint, and PostgreSQL is the safer default for most teams.
svg.desc: Redis persists checkpoints through a configurable append-only log or periodic snapshots and is constrained by RAM, eviction, and persistence settings; its best default is latency-sensitive, recoverable session state. PostgreSQL persists checkpoints through ACID transactions and a write-ahead log and is constrained by write latency and table growth; its best default is durable resume and reproducible debugging.

svg.text: Generic database benchmarks do not predict checkpoint performance — measure your own workload.
